messages:
Sara L: Heads-up — Equinox prod Dedicated pool started rejecting requests ~11:00 UTC. Customer reporting lots of 429s + big p95 latency spikes. I grabbed some logs and a quick metric snapshot below.

Anna (Support): On it. Can you confirm which pool? I already asked them for a replay of what they ran.

Sara L: Pool is dedicated-europe-2 (d-47). Customer says normal traffic ~200 TPS, spiked to ~2600 TPS for ~3m. Our metrics: admission_control started rejecting around 10:59:30 and burst_credit balance hit 0 at 10:59:20.

Kevin M: @infra-bot can you pull admission_control events + burst balance for d-47 between 10:56-11:06 UTC?

infra-bot: query accepted — returning condensed events: 
- 2026-03-15T10:58:45Z admission: ALLOW (tps 220)
- 2026-03-15T10:59:12Z admission: THROTTLE (tps 1.8k)
- 2026-03-15T10:59:20Z burst_balance: 0
- 2026-03-15T10:59:30Z admission: REJECT (reason=TPS_SLO_VIOLATION)
- 2026-03-15T10:59:30Z autoscaler: scale_attempt -> blocked (max_capacity_reached)
messages_addendum:
Sara L: customer attached a curl loop they ran after a failed job. snippet: 
```bash
for i in {1..5000}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-equinox" \
    -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.04
done
```

Anna (Support): they also said this started immediately after a partial replay of a nightly batch. Sounds like a client-side retry storm.

Mike R: Quick questions: were they at committed capacity? If max capacity is 4 GPUs and autoscaler won't exceed that, admission control will reject once burst buffer out.

Sara L: Yep, their Dedicated commit = 4 GPUs, autoscale.max = 4. The traffic would have needed ~8 gpus to keep latency at target.

Kevin M: Why did burst_balance hit 0? Shouldn't short spikes be absorbed?

infra-bot: Burst accounting: credits refill 100 tokens/hour. Their balance was low because there was a prior ~10m elevated traffic window at 08:30 — partial refill occurred but not full. Last refill timestamp: 2026-03-15T10:02:18Z. Credits consumed rapidly by this sudden replay.

Anna (Support): Customer is requesting emergency capacity and a refund/credit for the rejected requests. They want steps to avoid this happening again.

Mike R: Immediate action plan I propose: 
1) Hot-scale: temporarily increase pool to 6 GPUs to absorb backlog (ops).
2) Add short-term leniency in admission control for authenticated keys flagged as "customer-emergency"? Maybe dangerous. Safer: allow a one-time emergency manual override that consumes a separate emergency bucket.
3) Post-incident: update doc on headroom sizing and recommend customers set autoscale.max > committed to allow bursts.

Kevin M: Agreed. Also suggest we add server-side rate-limits per API key so a replay loop can't HTH their pool.

Sara L: @Mike R can you spin up 2 additional GPUs now? @Kevin M can you open an incident and include timeline + cost impact? I'll draft comms to the customer explaining what happened and immediate mitigations.

Mike R: Spinning now — ETA ~3m.

infra-bot: Action: created INC-2026-874 (dedicated overcommit + admission rejects). Snapshot: autoscale.policy = {"min":2,"max":4,"scale_step":1,"cooldown":120s}.

Kevin M: Incident created and assigned to eng-runtime. Adding timeline and raw logs.

Anna (Support): Customer confirmed they will pause the replay job. Also asked for guidance: recommended headroom formula?

Sara L: I'll propose: target_headroom = peak_expected_tps * safety_factor (1.5) mapped to GPU capacity using our perf table. Add a note to increase autoscale.max to at least 1.5x commit for batch-y workloads.

Mike R: Postmortem items: 
- Instrument burst credit depletion alert (currently only on 0) -> add early warning at 25%
- Add per-key replay detection (multiple identical small requests in short window) to surface to supp/ops
- Consider configurable short-lived emergency bucket for manual ops use

Kevin M: Also check billing: do we prorate or credit the customer for rejected requests? Finance liaison will weigh in.

Sara L: Thanks all. I'll send an initial status to the customer in 15m with actions and ETA for capacity. We'll reconvene in #incidents in 30m with the initial postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
